about: Routing policy for gearshift. Everything here is data: edit a copy and point GEARSHIFT_POLICY at it, or drop overrides in .gearshift.json. Patterns are case-insensitive regex fragments; the engine adds word boundaries on both ends.

lookup.what: Find files, grep, read logs, run tests and report, summarize long output
lookup.why: Read-only and verbose: the cost is input tokens, and a wrong answer is easy to spot. Haiku at its default effort; at low it is more likely to skip a search or stop early in agent loops.

extract.what: Classify, tag, extract fields, convert formats: single-shot, high-volume, checkable
extract.why: Simple high-volume requests are what Haiku at low effort is for, and outputs can be checked against a schema.

edit.what: A well-scoped change against a clear spec; a contained bug fix
edit.why: Sonnet is the everyday coding tier; medium is the documented starting effort for well-specified agentic coding.

write.what: Everyday documents, emails, summaries for people, slides, spreadsheets
write.why: Content creation is Sonnet territory; effort barely changes reply length, so medium is enough.

review.what: Review, investigation, analysis, comparison: repeated agent tasks that need judgment
review.why: Judgment work where missing something is the failure mode, so Sonnet runs at high (87.6% vs 80.3% at medium on SWE-bench Pro).

build.what: Multi-file features, tricky debugging, performance work, computer use, vision-heavy work
build.why: Opus at its default effort is Anthropic's recommended starting point for most agent workloads (92.8% at $0.22 per solved task on SWE-bench Pro).

design.what: Architecture, major refactors and migrations, complex systems engineering
design.why: Anthropic's selection matrix puts large-scale refactoring and complex systems engineering on Opus; high effort because a planning mistake is paid for by everything built on it.

research.what: Multistep deep research and analysis carried through to a finished report; leading other agents
research.why: On Anthropic's research benchmark Opus scored 2.4 points above Sonnet for 1.5x the cost, while Fable cost 4.3x Sonnet with no measurable gain; as an orchestrator Fable cost 19% more than Opus for about the same score.

frontier.what: The hardest reasoning: proofs, novel algorithms, scientific and quantitative work, problems smaller models already failed
frontier.why: The highest-capability tier, for when capability matters more than cost. Mostly a rung to climb to (Anthropic: move to Fable when Opus at xhigh still falls short); a starting point only when the brief says the problem is that hard. Most of its gain is already present at high.

chat.what: A conversational question a person is waiting on
chat.why: Latency-sensitive; the docs start chat at low or medium on Sonnet.

unsure.why: When unsure, Anthropic's guidance is to start on Opus at its default effort and optimize down later.

signals.name: explicit read-only instruction
patterns: (?:do not|don't|dont|never) (?:modify|edit|change|write|touch|alter) (?:any(?! other)|anything(?! else)|the code|code|files|the files|the repo\w*|the source)

signals.name: code refactor into a shared piece
patterns: into (?:a|one|its own|a shared|a separate|a single|a common) (?:\w+ )?(?:helper|function|module|method|class|component|file|hook|util\w*|package|library)

signals.name: many files or endpoints by count
list of three or more deliverables
migration or major refactor
patterns: tod[oa] (?:la base de c[oó]digo|el c[oó]digo|el repositorio|el sistema)
